chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Moving to Chicago, union rules, and the Benson Office jackets
summary: Chicago's union makes him work one-nighters for six months; the Benson booking office sends him out with rotating coloured jackets.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: No but listen - I went home.

Yeah, I went back to Defiance and, of course, uh, I had a taste of Cincinnati and I also got a look at Chicago and I wanted to go to Chicago. And, I think I went back to Cincinnati just to see Carl and the guys, from my home town. And, I was determined --- I was just determined that I wanted to -- I wanted to see what the hell everybody else was playing - what they were doing at this point. So, I went to Chicago, without a job and I had to put my union card in the union there and, uh, tell them that I wanted to come there and live. And, so, they rules and regulations and told me I couldn't work a steady job for six (6) months and I'd have to work only one night jobs; I couldn't take a job with the same band for two nights because that's considered a steady job.

Yeah. So, uh, I had start jobing--- so, at that point, I at least got to hear all the guys and where they were playing around Chicago and somebody told me that --- one of the guys around town said - why don't you go up to the Benson Office -- and tell them who you are and tell them you'd like to play in Chicago and you want to come here and live and, uh, tell them-- if they

want to know how you play - tell them, to send you out on one of those one nighters - at which they had at that time - they had little silk jackets that they gave different bands and, uh, of course, one of the regulations is - at that time - was they give you---you're with the yellow jackets tonight and tomorrow night you're with the pink jackets and then the white jackets and, you said - if I send you out - don't forget - there's no shaking hands on the job, (Laughter) because we don't want people to think that you guys haven't been together for a long time (laughter) -- you know, they had all kinds of these little rules -- and regulations.
Well, the Benson Office was just a booking office---
Yes but it was a big one.
